$comment: The pg_regress baseline (ADR-0001 decision 6): each test of the schedule on the pinned tag, run through the TCP bridge on the build, with --use-existing --max-connections=1. A failed test's normalised diff is regress/diffs/<test>.diff; an unstable test's outcome or diff differed between the recorded runs. `tests` and `summary` are written by `bun run regress --record`; `groups` (why each failing or unstable test fails) are written by hand and kept by --record. `bun run regress` fails on a new failure, a changed diff or a newly unstable test, and reports a vanished failure.

clock-resolution.reason: Unstable. The wasm's wall clock has millisecond resolution (Emscripten's clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME) reads Date.now()), so stats' `stats_reset > <the previous reset>` checks fail whenever two resets fall in the same millisecond. Its diff also carries single-process (no checkpointer, and checkpoint, WAL and I/O counters that do not move as it expects) and session-persistence (temp_buffers after \c).

extended-protocol-ready.reason: Unstable. An error in an extended-query batch sends a ReadyForQuery before the batch's Sync: pgl_longjmp (overlay pglite/src/pglitec/pglitec.c) sets send_ready_for_query before PostgresMainLongJmp sets ignore_till_sync, and PostgresMainLoopOnce sends it ahead of its next message. psql reports 'message type 0x5a arrived from server while idle' and then pairs results with the wrong queries; where it catches up depends on how the bytes are split between reads, so the diff differs from run to run.

icu-locales.reason: The only ICU collations are und-x-icu and unicode: initdb imports no language locale from the build's ICU data. collate.icu.utf8 skips itself only when there is no ICU collation at all, so it runs and fails on en-x-icu, sv-x-icu, tr-x-icu, ….

regress-library.reason: The tests' C functions are missing (binary_coercible, widget_in, interpt_pp, test_enc_setup, test_enc_conversion, make_tuple_indirect, trigger_return_old, test_fdw_handler, …), and so is everything built on them (the widget type, the iexit view, the test foreign-data wrapper, opr_sanity's binary_coercible checks, conversion's test_enc_* checks). The run's --dlpath holds no regress.so: the build tree's own src/test/regress/regress.so is not a module the build ships, so pglite.wasm does not export 29 of its imports (IsBinaryCoercible, pg_do_encoding_conversion_buf, lseg_intersect, cpu_operator_cost, …) and its dlopen fails, and in this runtime a failed dlopen breaks every later one. Without the file, CREATE FUNCTION … AS :'regresslib' fails with 'could not access file' before any dlopen. conversion's diff also shows session-authorization (DROP USER after RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION).

session-authorization.reason: RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION does not return to the superuser. Single-user mode (InitializeSessionUserIdStandalone) never gives the session_authorization setting a value, so its reset value is empty and RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION (like SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT) changes nothing: after a test's first SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION, the rest of the test runs as that role, and ownership, privilege and role-management errors follow (and objects the test cannot drop). The bridge's reset sets the superuser back explicitly, so it ends with the test. alter_table's diff also shows start-parameters (-O).

session-persistence.reason: psql's \c gets the same backend back: the bridge resets the session instead of starting a new one. Login event triggers never fire (event_trigger_login), temp_buffers cannot be changed once any temporary table was used in the backend (temp, and stats), and plpgsql, loaded by an earlier test, already reserves its prefix (guc, which then also shows session-authorization). temp's PREPARE TRANSACTION also finds prepared transactions disabled: max_prepared_transactions is 0, where pg_regress's own temporary instance sets 2.

single-process.reason: One embedded backend and no other process: no checkpointer, no background or parallel workers. The start parameters set max_worker_processes, max_parallel_workers and max_parallel_workers_per_gather to 0, so plans that expect the default of 2 have no Gather (partition_prune, plpgsql's debug_parallel_query), and select_parallel's own settings launch no worker. stats shows it too (see clock-resolution).

start-parameters.reason: The backend runs with PGlite's start parameters (the driver's START_PARAMS): search_path=public instead of "$user", public shows a table in the role's own schema qualified (create_schema). -O (allow_system_table_mods) also lets alter_table change system catalogs where it expects to be refused (alter_table, in session-authorization).

walreceiver-libpq.reason: libpqwalreceiver.so loads, and CREATE SUBSCRIPTION … WITH (connect = false) works, but a connection attempt fails with 'libpq is incorrectly linked to backend functions' where 'port=-1' expects libpq's own 'invalid port number': the module links libpq statically without libpgcommon's frontend build, so libpq's pg_link_canary_is_frontend() is the backend's, which says no (and libpq's pg_char_to_encoding and pg_encoding_to_char stay unresolved, since the backend has them only as *_private). Its diff also shows session-authorization (the role tests at its end), and it is unstable through clock-resolution: in some runs (3 of 8 when recorded) two pg_stat_reset_subscription_stats calls fall in the same millisecond, so the second stats_reset is not later.

wasm-stack.reason: check_stack_depth() measures the wasm's shadow stack, which holds only the locals whose address is taken, and the JSON parser's recursion takes none: with max_stack_depth at 100kB, 10000 nested levels never trip it, and json and jsonb report the unterminated input ('invalid input syntax for type json') instead of 'stack depth limit exceeded'. The bridge's raised native stack (256 MiB, see scripts/lib/regress/run.ts) keeps the recursion from overflowing the host's stack first, so the result no longer depends on how far JavaScriptCore has compiled the wasm: on the default stack json and jsonb were unstable, and infinite_recurse threw out of the wasm; it passes now.
